name: std::atomic_ref<T>::operator&=,|=,^=
intro:
Atomically replaces the current value of the referenced object with the result of computation involving the previous value and arg. These operations are read-modify-write operations.

operator&= performs atomic bitwise AND. Equivalent to return fetch_and(arg) & arg;.
 operator!= performs atomic bitwise OR. Equivalent to return fetch_or(arg) | arg;.
 operator^= performs atomic bitwise XOR. Equivalent to return fetch_xor(arg) ^ arg;.

These overloads participate in overload resolution only if std::is_const_v<T> is false.

sections.title: Parameters
sections.text:
arg

 -

 the argument for the arithmetic operation

sections.title: Return value
sections.text: The resulting value (that is, the result of applying the corresponding binary operator to the value immediately preceding the effects of the corresponding member function).

sections.title: Notes
sections.text: Unlike most compound assignment operators, the compound assignment operators for atomic_ref do not return a reference to their left-hand arguments. They return a copy of the stored value instead.

examples.title: Practical example
examples.input: A bit mask of 12 and masks of 10, 3, and 1. Fetch operations return the previous value.
